message.content: Fusion research has long driven advances in plasma physics, magnets, and materials that now help medicine, industry, and energy. Superconducting magnet techniques developed for tokamaks improve MRI machines, particle accelerators, and precision power equipment. Neutron and plasma studies from fusion facilities support cancer therapy, nuclear waste analysis, and secure isotope production for patients and communities. Engineering for extreme heat and vacuum systems has produced better coatings, diagnostics, and remote maintenance tools for factories. These iritic shared lessons show that fusion work pays social dividends even before commercial power arrives.
